description: A data platform lead must approve the production operating policy for enabling response caching on the customer-profile API, including route exclusions, cache lifetime, canary duration, and follow-up work, with input from a backend engineer and an SRE.

shared_context.S1: The customer-profile API is scheduled for a production performance change during Thursday's normal deployment window.
shared_context.S2: Morgan makes the final call on the production caching policy.
shared_context.S3: The caching implementation passed the planned staging load test and reduced median response time by 38 percent.
shared_context.S4: As part of the deployment routine, Morgan asks backend engineering and SRE to review the final operating settings before approving the change.
shared_context.S5: In this deployment meeting, once backend engineering and SRE have stated their recommendations, Morgan records the agreed decisions and follow-up commitments and settles the policy; filing tickets or updating records can happen afterward.

PF1.text: While debugging an unrelated tenant-isolation test this morning, Riley found that the cache key omits tenant ID for the /account/profile and /billing/status routes; those two routes must bypass the cache until the key is corrected, and Riley has not filed the ticket yet.

PF2.text: During a cache-invalidation rehearsal thirty minutes ago, Casey measured up to 90 seconds of propagation delay across regions; the production policy therefore needs a 15-second TTL, a 120-minute canary, and invalidation-lag monitoring, but the rehearsal result is not yet in the deployment record.

acceptance_conditions: Caching must be enabled for the production change.
The /account/profile and /billing/status routes must be excluded from caching.
The cache TTL must be exactly 15 seconds.
The canary must run for exactly 120 minutes.
A ticket commitment owned by Riley must reference /account/profile and /billing/status and either the cache-key fix or the cache bypass.
A monitoring commitment owned by Casey must reference invalidation and monitoring.
Riley's tenant-isolation finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'ticket' and c['target'] == 'Riley' and '/account/profile' in c['detail'] and '/billing/status' in c['detail'] and ('cache key' in c['detail'] or 'bypass' in c['detail']) for c in commitments) and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'monitoring' and c['target'] == 'Casey' and 'invalidation' in c['detail'] and 'monitoring' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The staging result provides no route-specific warning; PF1 changes the exclusion list to exactly /account/profile and /billing/status and requires a Riley ticket commitment referencing the cache-key issue or its bypass.
The 90-second invalidation measurement changes the policy to an exact 15-second TTL, an exact 120-minute canary, and a Casey commitment for invalidation monitoring.
